name: Beat Jans
bio: Beat Anton Jans is a Swiss environmental scientist and Social Democratic (SP/PS) politician who has served on the Federal Council since 1 January 2024, heading the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP/DFJP). He represents the canton of Basel-Stadt. Born on 12 July 1964 in Basel and raised in a working-class family in Riehen, Jans first trained and qualified as a farmer (1985), then earned an agricultural-technician diploma at the Technikum for Tropical Agriculture of the Swiss Tropical Institute in Basel (1987) and a degree in Environmental Sciences from ETH Zurich (1994). He worked in development cooperation with Helvetas in Haiti and Paraguay (1987-1989), then for the nature-conservation organisation Pro Natura (1995-2010), where he became head of the Politics and International department and a member of the management board, and later as a sustainability and communications consultant. He joined the SP in 1998, presided over the SP Basel-Stadt (2000-2005), sat in the Grand Council of Basel-Stadt (2001-2011), and served on the National Council (2010-2020), where he was a member of the environment/energy and economics committees and vice-president of the SP Switzerland (2015-2020). Elected to the Basel-Stadt cantonal government in 2020, he was President of the Government (Regierungspraesident) of Basel-Stadt from 2021 to 2023. On 13 December 2023 the United Federal Assembly elected him to the Federal Council on the third ballot (134 of 245 valid votes) to succeed Alain Berset. As Justice Minister his policy focus has included asylum and migration, combating violence against women, and Switzerland-EU relations.
